## limitations

The session serves operations only after Ghidra reports default auto-analysis complete; incomplete analysis does not expose partial results.,The imported Program and temporary project are ephemeral and deleted on close. Annotation operations edit session database metadata; original executable bytes are never written.,Cancelling an active Ghidra request terminates its ephemeral database and discards session annotations. The selected target remains open; the next provider query imports the original artifact again.,Default-space addresses use lowercase 0x-prefixed hexadecimal; other address spaces use <percent-encoded-space>:0x<hex>.,References cover the complete Ghidra function-body AddressSet and exact entry. Dossier incoming edges omit sources owned by that function; procedure_references also retains those internal edges.,The dossier combines Ghidra FunctionManager, Listing, ReferenceManager, BasicBlockModel, and decompiler observations; provider-specific pseudocode and assembly are not cross-provider text invariants.,Resolved reference metadata identifies computed, indirect, external, call, jump, and data edges; unresolved targetless flows remain unknown, and function classifications distinguish thunks and externals.,Synthetic Ghidra entry-point references without actionable memory sources are omitted.,The Java bridge serializes one function request per Program and lets each decompilation run until it completes or the caller cancels.,Ghidra Listing reports a terminal call at 0x1402a7ad6 with no resolved callee; its no-return basis is unknown.,Windows Ghidra P0 accepts approved native x86 and x86-64 PE applications and DLLs; managed, hostile, sensitive, and mutable-path targets are unsupported.,The Windows bridge uses authenticated IPv4 loopback because Node path-based IPC does not expose Java AF_UNIX sockets; the endpoint file contains no bearer token.,Windows sessions require the matching packaged Windows x64 native addon, local NTFS targets and runtimes, and Windows 10 or later.
